parts.text: The IGCSE class is investigating the stretching of a spring. Fig. 1.1 shows the experimental set up. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 1.1, measure the vertical distance d 0 , in mm, between the bottom of the spring and the surface of the bench. d 0 = .......................................... mm [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The diagram is drawn 1/10 th actual size. Calculate the actual distance D 0 , in mm, between the bottom of the spring and the surface of the bench. D 0 = .......................................... mm [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) A student hangs a 1.0 N load on the spring. He measures and records the distance D between the bottom of the spring and the surface of the bench, and the value of the load L . He repeats the procedure using loads of 2.0 N, 3.0 N, 4.0 N and 5.0 N. The distance readings are shown in Table 1.1. Calculate the extension e of the spring, for each set of readings, using the equation e = ( D 0 – D ). Record the values of L and e in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 L / N D / mm e / mm 199 191 179 171 160 [2]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Plot a graph of e / mm ( y -axis) against L / N ( x -axis). [4]

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ..................................................[2]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) When making measurements, the student is careful to avoid a line-of-sight error. Suggest one other precaution that the student should take when measuring the distance D between the bottom of the spring and the surface of the bench. .......................................................................................................................................... ......................................................................................................................................[1]
